title: American Garlic Bread
subtitle: Buttery, herbed garlic bread baked in the oven
excerpt: American garlic bread is a halved baguette or Italian loaf spread generously with garlic butter, wrapped in foil and baked until the butter melts through, then opened and returned to the oven to crisp. It goes with pasta, pizza, soup, or salad.
sourceNotes: American garlic bread evolved from Italian-American cooking as a side for pasta and pizza. The foil-wrap method is the home standard, producing soft bread with a slightly crunchy open face.

recipe.freezeNotes: Assemble the buttered loaf, wrap in foil, and freeze before baking. Bake from frozen at 180°C for 25 minutes foil-on, then 5 minutes open.
recipe.batchNotes: Make several loaves at once: they bake well side by side.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble and wrap in foil. Refrigerate for up to 24 hours before baking.

content.text: American garlic bread is a halved baguette or Italian loaf spread thickly with garlic butter, wrapped in foil, and baked until soft and steaming inside. The foil comes off for the last five minutes so the cut face gets a little colour. It takes ten minutes to assemble and twenty minutes in the oven.

items.prepNote: or a ciabatta or Italian bread loaf

content.text: Make the garlic butter and assemble
Heat the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C / gas mark 4). Combine {{unsalted-butter}}, {{garlic}}, {{parsley-flat}}, and {{sea-salt-flakes}} in a small bowl and mix well until smooth.
Slice the {{baguette}} in half lengthways. Spread the garlic butter generously and evenly across both cut halves, going right to the edges. If using {{parmesan}}, scatter it over the butter.
Sandwich the halves back together. Wrap the whole loaf tightly in foil, folding the seam over at the top. Place on a baking tray.
Bake at 180°C for 15 minutes, foil on. Open the foil to expose the cut face and return to the oven for a further five minutes until the edges are slightly crisp and golden.
Pull apart into portions at the table or cut into thick slices. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: The butter is pooling in the foil rather than soaking into the bread
items.cause: Butter wasn't soft enough to spread evenly, or spread too thickly.
items.fix: The butter must be really soft (spreadable with a knife without tearing the bread). Mix it thoroughly with the garlic and herbs so it spreads in a thin, even layer.

items.symptom: The cut face is pale and soft after uncovering
items.cause: Oven not hot enough, or too little time uncovered.
items.fix: For the last five minutes, switch on the grill element as well, which will colour the surface quickly. Watch it closely.

items.symptom: The garlic tastes raw and harsh
items.cause: Raw garlic can be overpowering, especially if freshly crushed.
items.fix: Use the flat side of a knife to crush the garlic to a paste with a pinch of salt. This breaks down the harsh compounds. Alternatively, swap to garlic powder (half a teaspoon) for a milder flavour.

items.symptom: The bread is soggy in the middle
items.cause: Too much butter for the size of the loaf, or a very dense bread.
items.fix: A thinner, crisper baguette-style loaf works better than a dense Italian bread. The foil hold the steam in: 15 minutes is usually enough, but check by pressing the loaf through the foil.

content.text: Garlic bread in the American style is a fixture of Italian-American restaurant tables, sent out before the pasta arrives. The foil-wrap method developed in home kitchens as a way to make it in advance and keep it warm. It's simpler than the Italian bruschetta tradition (which uses toasted dry bread rubbed with raw garlic) and feeds more people from one loaf. Serve alongside pasta dishes, pizza, soups, or a large green salad.
